subject: IPv6 overlay rehearsal and dual‑stack acceptance for upcoming on‑prem cutover
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Bowers <alex.bowers@nimbushosting.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: IPv6 overlay rehearsal and dual‑stack acceptance for upcoming on‑prem cutover

Team —

As we prep for the on‑prem cutover next week, I want to run a focused rehearsal for the IPv6 overlay + dual‑stack acceptance flow. Goal is to validate the runbook steps that touch:

- IPv6 subnet assignment and route propagation
- Overlay tunnel establishment (WireGuard) between edge and Nimbus colo
- Health‑check traffic (KV cache warmup + small generation traffic) over IPv6 paths
- Fallback behavior when IPv6 path is degraded (auto‑switch to IPv4 via smart routing)

Please use the attached runbook (runbook-ipv6-overlay-v2.md) and drop logs into the shared folder. Specific asks:

1) Dev — can you take the lead on the tunnel bring‑up and smoke generation (10k tokens across 50 requests) and capture kernel/mss adjustments you apply?
2) Irene — please validate route distribution and BGP adjacency on the on‑prem border, note any asymmetric route observations.
3) Marcus — observe traffic shaping rules on the egress fabric and confirm alarms fire correctly on 95th percentile thresholds.

Alex / Nimbus — can your team stand by for BGP peering check and confirm you see our IPv6 prefixes once tunnels are live?

Plan: start rehearsal 14:00 UTC today, 60 minute window. If we see anything blocking, we capture remediation steps in the runbook and decide go/no‑go for the full cutover rehearsal on Friday.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Manager, Private Deployments 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-ipv6-overlay-v2.md, ipv6-subnet-plan.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Alex Bowers <alex.bowers@nimbushosting.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: IPv6 overlay rehearsal and dual‑stack acceptance for upcoming on‑prem cutover

Quick update from the 14:00 UTC window — major steps completed, flagged a couple items:

Summary:
- WireGuard tunnels established between on‑prem edge and Nimbus colo; handshake stable after MTU tweak (mss clamping to 1350).
- IPv6 prefixes propagated to Nimbus and visible via v6 route table.
- Performed KV cache warmup: 50 requests, ~9.8k tokens total, median tail latency over IPv6 42ms.
- Smart routing fallback test: intentionally dropped IPv6 path on our side — traffic failed over to IPv4 within 6s as expected.

Issues / Notes:
1) BGP flap observed for 120s during initial tunnel bring‑up — seems tied to a misadvertised next‑hop on our border. Irene, see the annotated bgp dump attached.
2) Observability: our IPv6 telemetry keys were not collecting the interface name — missed one heatmap slot in the first 10 minutes. Patch submitted (PR #1342) to the agent.

Attachments: rehearsal-log-20261118.txt (contains timestamps, tcpdump snippets, bgp dumps), snippet: /drive/1a2b3c-ipv6-rehearsal/logs/rehearsal-log-20261118.txt

Next steps: we will re‑run corrected tunnel bring‑up at 18:30 UTC and replay the warmup torrent. If that passes, we update runbook with MTU clamp and bgp workarounds then mark the overlay acceptance as "validated‑needle" and proceed to Friday's full cutover rehearsal.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Alex Bowers <alex.bowers@nimbushosting.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: IPv6 overlay rehearsal and dual‑stack acceptance for upcoming on‑prem cutover

Adding detail on the BGP flap and route asymmetry:

- Root cause: one of the border devices had an old static route pointing to a decommissioned interface; when tunnel endpoints flapped, that static route briefly won over iBGP due to administrative distance. Cleared the stale static and reloaded BGP session.
- Verified with Nimbus that they saw the prefix withdraw and reannounce; no evidence the prefixes were black‑holed.
- Action added to runbook: pre‑check step to validate no stale statics and run a one‑line BGP sanity on each border device (command snippet included).

I will re‑run the adjacency check during the 18:30 UTC run and paste bgp summary after.

Irene
Irene Choi
Network Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Bowers <alex.bowers@nimbushosting.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 18:01:00 -0000
Subject: Re: IPv6 overlay rehearsal and dual‑stack acceptance for upcoming on‑prem cutover

Thanks for the heads up — Nimbus team confirmed:
- We saw the initial withdraw then reannounce for your /48; our edge held traffic and no customer impact.
- Peering timers stable after the reload.
- Observability: we saw completion of the KV warmup across IPv6; tail latency matches your metrics.

Two small requests from our side:
1) Can you include the WireGuard endpoint fingerprints in the final runbook excerpt so our ops can verify identity quickly?
2) Share the exact time windows you will trigger traffic mirroring during Friday's rehearsal so we can correlate with our packet captures.

Happy to be on the bridge Friday.

— Alex
Alex Bowers
Senior Cloud Network Engineer
Nimbus Hosting

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Bowers <alex.bowers@nimbushosting.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: IPv6 overlay rehearsal and dual‑stack acceptance for upcoming on‑prem cutover — decision and runbook updates

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. After reviewing logs and Nexrad-style correlation from Nimbus, we are marking the IPv6 overlay rehearsal as "conditional‑acceptance":

- Tunnel stability validated with MTU clamp documented.
- BGP static cleanup step added to runbook (preflight check), bgp summary snippet included.
- Smart routing fallback validated within SLA (<=10s).
- Observability gap patched; telemetry tag added to agent PR #1342.

Action items before Friday full rehearsal:
1) Marcus — confirm egress shaping thresholds test harness is in Canary for Friday.
2) Dev — include WireGuard fingerprints and the exact 10min mirroring windows for Friday (add to runbook and post to Drive).
3) Irene — run final border preflight script and paste results to Jira NETOPS-8721 by EOD Thursday.

If the above are green, we'll proceed with the 11/22 full cutover rehearsal (14:00–15:30 UTC) and invite Nimbus to the bridge at 13:45 UTC. If any item is red, we'll hold and reconvene Monday.

Appended: quick diff of runbook (runbook-ipv6-overlay-v2.md) includes the MTU clamp step, BGP preflight, and observability checklist.

Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
